profiles.meeting_scenario: A university-affiliated medical AI lab is holding a planning meeting to prepare a 6-week internal replication-and-extension sprint based on a published melanoma recognition approach that combines transferred deep features, sparse coding, and an SVM on the ISIC dermoscopy dataset. The immediate context is that the team wants a reproducible benchmark package for an upcoming grant progress review and a draft methods appendix for a workshop submission. The agenda is to decide what exactly will be reproduced first, what artifacts will be delivered at the end of the sprint, how the data split and evaluation loop will be operationalized, who owns each workstream, and what timeline checkpoints to use. The expected outcome is a shared plan covering experiment setup, implementation responsibilities, evaluation packaging, and a final 'replication baseline' deliverable.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Medical image analysis, representation learning, reproducible benchmarking
members.background: Maya leads methodological replication projects in an academic biomedical AI lab and previously worked on transfer learning pipelines for radiology and dermatology datasets.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, defensible replication package that can survive reviewer scrutiny with minimal custom engineering, and she is quietly worried that timeline slippage will leave them with results that are hard to document or justify.
hidden_assumptions: A 'replication baseline' means reproducing the full headline evaluation package from the paper, including both discrimination tasks and the repeated two-fold cross-validation regime summarized in aggregate form.

The 'ISIC set' for this sprint refers to the exact curated subset already mirrored in the lab's benchmark storage, with prior filtering and lesion-level deduplication preserved from earlier internal work.

When they say the pipeline will be 'frozen' before the main runs, that freeze applies to code and preprocessing choices before launching the 20 repeated two-fold evaluation cycles, not merely before drafting the write-up.

A 'results table' means one publication-style summary table with averaged accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and significance numbers across the repeated runs rather than a fold-by-fold artifact bundle.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.expertise: Experiment pipelines, data tooling, model training infrastructure
members.background: Alex supports research teams by turning papers into executable pipelines and has recently built containerized workflows for computer vision benchmarks using dermatology image archives.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the sprint operationally simple by reusing existing infrastructure, avoid bespoke data handling, and produce artifacts that can later feed into automation, while quietly protecting his team from open-ended analysis requests.
hidden_assumptions: A 'replication baseline' means getting the main melanoma-vs-rest experiment running end-to-end first, with the second discrimination task treated as an extension if time permits.

The 'ISIC set' means the current raw export from the institution's synced ISIC bucket, where image-level records are the unit of processing unless someone explicitly requests historical filtering rules.

When the team says the pipeline should be 'frozen,' that means API shape and container dependencies are stable before broader handoff; numerical settings can still be tuned until the final reporting pass.

A 'results table' should be backed by stored outputs for each split and run, because downstream users will expect per-run logs and machine-readable metrics rather than only a publication-style aggregate.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the replication baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly refer to delivering the 'replication baseline' for the paper.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the baseline includes both published discrimination tasks: melanoma vs all non-melanoma lesions and melanoma vs atypical lesions only.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the baseline is the main melanoma-vs-rest task, while the atypical-only comparison is a stretch goal or follow-on extension.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both tasks are described in the paper, and calling the work a 'baseline' sounds naturally shared; because both participants are cooperative and pressed for planning efficiency, neither feels a need to restate the exact boundary of what baseline includes.

misalignment_points.topic: Which ISIC dataset instance they mean
misalignment_points.surface_form: They mention using 'the ISIC set' and 'the 2,624-case dataset' as if it were a single obvious object.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the lab's previously curated 2,624-case lesion-level benchmark subset matched to the paper's case counts after internal filtering and deduplication.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the currently synced ISIC archive export from which he expects to derive approximately that cohort, likely at image level and without assuming prior historical filters unless specified.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The same headline case count and dataset name create a strong illusion of shared reference, and both assume the other is invoking the standard institutional resource they personally use most often.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to freeze the pipeline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the pipeline should be 'frozen' before the main runs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means methodological freeze: preprocessing, split logic, and model settings should stop changing before the 20 repeated two-fold cross-validation repetitions begin so the benchmark remains reviewable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means deployment freeze: containers, interfaces, and job orchestration should stabilize for handoff, while hyperparameters and small preprocessing tweaks can continue until the reporting pass.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In technical teams, 'freeze' is a familiar planning term, but it is used in both research-governance and engineering-operations senses; the overlap makes each interpretation feel obvious and not worth unpacking.

misalignment_points.topic: What the final results package should contain
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss producing the 'results table' and say it should be ready for the review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 will consider the deliverable complete if there is a polished paper-style summary table with aggregate means and significance statements for the repeated experiments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 will consider it complete only if the table is generated from archived per-run outputs, split manifests, and machine-readable metrics suitable for reuse in the lab pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both a polished summary and a reproducible artifact bundle are normal components of successful research delivery, so saying 'results table' gives a feeling of alignment while masking different completion standards.

I need this framed as a bounded, proper replication so we do not drift into custom engineering that becomes impossible to document cleanly.
